Messages.Author: Shawn F. Carnes
Messages.Body:
I know I'm making some calls before the RT meets 8/21, but I actually
know some of these answers! :)

1} Strike: Combat Ends (S:CE)
-----------------------------
* When dealing with S:CE, combat stops immediately. No further strikes,
additional strikes, or presses are resolved.
* Both minions may declare strikes, but S:CE takes the lead in all
resolution.
* In respect to Riposte vs. Majesty, the S:CE by the acting minion is
resolved first. If it is Riposte, the opposing minion does take the
damage. If it is Majesty (played by the acting minion), the acting
minion will not take damage from Riposte.

LOGIC: My logic in this is that strike resolution is seperate from
strike declaration. You can declare it and pay for it all day long, but
resolution is another entirely different manner.

2} Alexandra
------------
* Alexandra may use her ability to tap or untap a Toreador anytime
during your turn. This does include bringing her out during your
influence phase.

LOGIC: Pretty straightforward here. The text reads, "Once during your
turn..." This signifies to me that, if ready, she can do it whenever
you wish during your turn. Influence, though after the minion phase, is
still during your turn.

--

>LOGIC: My logic in this is that strike resolution is seperate from

You LOGIC fails to explain why the acting minion's strike resolves before
the blocking (or opposing) minion's strike. If the actor's Riposte beats
the defender's Riposte, why doesn't the actor's Claws (or other agg. strike)
beat the defender's Claws? Stop making exceptions that make no sense.

The actor decalres his strike first to give the defender an advantage;
resolving that strike first (when both strikes have been explicitly stated
to resolve simultaneously) is just a knee-jerk "ruling" made without
much thought (IMNSHO).

>2} Alexandra
>------------
>* Alexandra may use her ability to tap or untap a Toreador anytime
>during your turn. This does include bringing her out during your
>influence phase.

>LOGIC: Pretty straightforward here. The text reads, "Once during your
>turn..." This signifies to me that, if ready, she can do it whenever
>you wish during your turn. Influence, though after the minion phase, is
>still during your turn.

Excelent interpretation of the missing "only" modifier here.
Can we get a similar ruling on Master:Out-of-Turn and/or 2nd Tradition? :-)

so much a strike as it is something that happens in place of a strike

This makes perfect sense, you need to remember that taking agg damage
is not like playing combat-ends as a strike. You go to torper during

the blocker, your strike does nothing. Both strikes happened, no more
strikes will this combat. With Strike: Combat Ends, combat ends right then
and there, you can decide your strike, but you do not get to the strike

None of this explains what happens when BOTH minions use Riposte to
end combat in the second round (which is what that little snippet of
my post above (the first two lines) is referencing (now out of context).

Both announce Riposte as their strike (first actor, then defender).
Both strikes are S:CE.
The strikes resolve simultaneously (by the rulebook).

Why has the Rules Team ruled that only the acting minion's Riposte resolves?
(Because it resolves first; before the defenders strike; *not* simultaneously;
in dirrect contradiction to the rulebook).

(The bit about claws (which had been cut from the quoted text) was
illustrating that, if BOTH minion's strikes are claws, then they resolve
simultaneously (as stated in rulebook). If the acting minion's Claws
resolved first in this case (as the Rules Team says that S:CE does), then
the defender would be in torpor before his (ostensibly simulatenous) strike
could resolve.)

Messages.Body:

Scott Johnson) writes:

>None of this explains what happens when BOTH minions use Riposte to
>end combat in the second round (which is what that little snippet of
>my post above (the first two lines) is referencing (now out of context).
>
>Both announce Riposte as their strike (first actor, then defender).
>Both strikes are S:CE.
>The strikes resolve simultaneously (by the rulebook).

No. The rule book says that if the acting minion plays S:CE then the
blocker can play a strike, but the blocker's strike will have no effect.
See page 30 under Combat Ends.
